hook: Hans Moravec was born in Kautzen, Austria, in 1948 and moved to Canada as a child, earning a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Acadia University in 1969 and a master's in computer science from the University of Western Ontario in 1971. He completed a Ph.D. in computer science at Stanford University in 1980, building an early mobile robot that used a television camera and an onboard computer to navigate cluttered rooms. He then joined Carnegie Mellon University, where he directed the Mobile Robot Laboratory at the Robotics Institute for twenty-five years, developing three-dimensional occupancy grid mapping that let robots build spatial maps from noisy sensor data. In his 1988 book Mind Children, he observed that tasks requiring abstract reasoning are computationally easy for machines while tasks requiring basic sensorimotor skills, such as walking or recognizing a face, are extremely hard, an observation now known as Moravec's paradox. In 2003 he co-founded Seegrid Corporation to commercialize automated guided vehicle technology built on his mapping research, serving as its chief scientist.
name: Hans Moravec

quote.text: It is comparatively easy to make computers exhibit adult level performance on intelligence tests or playing checkers, and difficult or impossible to give them the skills of a one-year-old when it comes to perception and mobility.
quote.context: Mind Children: The Future of Robot and Human Intelligence (1988), stating what became known as Moravec's paradox

quick_facts: Born in Kautzen, Austria, in 1948, and earned degrees in Canada before completing a Ph.D. at Stanford in 1980
Directed the Mobile Robot Laboratory at Carnegie Mellon University's Robotics Institute for twenty-five years
Developed three-dimensional occupancy grid mapping for robot navigation
Formulated Moravec's paradox in Mind Children (1988): abstract reasoning is easy for computers, sensorimotor skills are hard
Co-founded Seegrid Corporation in 2003 to commercialize automated guided vehicle technology
Author of Mind Children (1988) and Robot: Mere Machine to Transcendent Mind (1999)

achievements.title: Three-dimensional occupancy grid mapping
achievements.impact: Gave mobile robots a way to build usable spatial maps from noisy sonar and camera data, a technique still used in robot navigation and self-driving vehicles.

achievements.title: Moravec's paradox (Mind Children, 1988)
achievements.impact: Identified that high-level reasoning is computationally cheap while basic sensorimotor skills are extremely expensive for machines, reversing the assumption that intelligence tests measure what is hardest to automate.

achievements.title: Mobile Robot Laboratory, Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute
achievements.impact: Built and directed one of the first dedicated mobile robotics research labs, training a generation of roboticists over twenty-five years.

achievements.title: Seegrid Corporation (2003)
achievements.impact: Co-founded a company that commercialized vision-guided automated vehicles for warehouses and factories, applying his mapping research to industry.
